items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: He would mention, he said, Monk had some really hip

ctx.x: Were those fellows making any — hmm — were they making any money working with Sun Ra or was it more like this is just something I really need to do?

Well they were making money. Let me see, now John Gilmore, he had a choice. Well he did, he played with Mingus, he played with Art Blakey. He recorded with Art Blakey. And he could have gone and been out there and played in the band but the music that Sun Ra was writing and creating was so challenging. That’s what kept him into Sun Ra’s music. He would mention, he said, Monk had some really hip and but he said he was more interested in what Sun Ra was doing harmonically in those intervals. And the reason, I don’t…

paid and then whatever portion of their rent, you know, went in. So I never truly understand it. But one thing I did know and I can say, Sun Ra never had a bank account so he dealt — most of his money was in cash — ten thousand — I remember going to Europe and Sun Ra would have these kind of dashiki things he had made these clothes, and he had a money belt. And I used to see that and I’ve seen his money belt. And he would have all of his money on him or somewhere, and then he always had members of the band around…
